physical.physical_description: Sarong of cotton batik. The sarong is sewn into a tube with the kepala (front panel) of dark blue with brown and white tumpals, and with a dark blue Chinese influenced floral pattern. The main field is covered with a geometric design of dark red squares with blue centres arranged in a trellis pattern.
physical.summary: This sarong is sewn into a tube with the kepala (front panel) in dark blue with brown and white tumpals and a dark blue Chinese influenced floral pattern. The main field is covered with a geometric design of dark red squares with blue centres arranged in a trellis pattern. There is a strong Indian incluence in the colours. The sarong is associated with Jambi, southern Sumatra, and was almost certainly made there, although the suggestion has been made that such cloths were made in Java for export to Sumatra.

physical.physical_description: Sarong of cotton batik. The cotton is waxed with the tjanting and copper blocks, and dyed indigo, brown and red on a cream ground. The field is patterned with large stylised flowering leafy branches, repeated horizontally, with a butterfly at one end of each row. The head (kepala) and borders are patterned with stylised animals, birds, insects and plants.

physical.physical_description: Sarong (Kain Pandjang) of cotton batik. Cotton waxed with the tjanting and dyed indigo and light brown with white reserved. The field is patterned with stylised objects, predominantly wing (lar) and snake (naga) motifs, repeated on a background of conventional leaves. The head (kepala) and borders are patterned with a foliage (semen) motif,  The intervals between the triangles (tumpal) of the kepala have conventional rosettes reserved.
